title: Machine-learning-guided proteomics identifies APOC3, RAB39A and KNG1 for plaque-rupture classification in acute coronary syndrome
summary: In an acute-coronary-syndrome derivation cohort matched for plaque rupture (PR) versus intact fibrous cap (IFC), quantitative mass spectrometry measured 1,121 plasma proteins. Five machine-learning algorithms screened candidate proteins; APOC3, RAB39A and KNG1 were then significantly different between PR and IFC in an independent 85-patient cohort using ELISA. The three proteins discriminated plaque rupture better than the study’s conventional biomarkers and risk factors, suggesting a candidate biomarker panel for identifying PR among ACS patients.
ai_technology: Unbiased machine-learning feature screening of quantitative mass-spectrometry plasma proteomics using five algorithms
organization: Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Capital Medical University; Beijing Institute of Heart Lung and Blood Vessel Diseases; First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University

evidence.tested: In an acute-coronary-syndrome derivation cohort matched for plaque rupture (PR) versus intact fibrous cap (IFC), quantitative mass spectrometry measured 1,121 plasma proteins.
evidence.unknown: This was a small matched derivation cohort (110 ACS patients) and an 85-patient validation cohort, not prospective outcome prediction or a clinical-impact trial. The proteins are candidate diagnostic markers; the study does not show that using them improves management or outcomes, nor establish causal roles in plaque rupture. The publisher reports electronic publication 2024-08-06 and issue date 2024-09-15; the record uses online-first date.
evidence.ai_role: The ML algorithms selected nine candidate proteins from the proteomic measurements; the study subsequently tested candidates in an independent ACS cohort and confirmed three analytes—APOC3, RAB39A and KNG1—as significantly different in plaque-rupture versus intact-cap groups. ELISA provided the independent protein validation. The AI-enabled result is this prioritized, externally tested three-protein panel for a specific plaque phenotype.
